title: Halting on an encoded pair
statement: Let $c$ be a machine representation scheme and let $\alpha$ and $x$ be bit strings. The halting function of $c$ returns true on the pairing encoding of $\alpha$ and $x$ if and only if the machine decoded from $\alpha$ produces some output on input $x$ within some finite number of steps.
replaced:
Let $c$ be a coding scheme for Turing machines and let $\alpha$ and $x$ be bit
strings. Then $\mathrm{HALT}_c$, evaluated on the pairing encoding
$\langle \alpha, x \rangle$, is true if and only if the machine that $\alpha$
denotes under $c$ halts on input $x$, completing some output within some finite
number of steps.
